lesson.title: IJ / UI / OE Gym
lesson.subtitle: ice, out, thousand, brown, mouse, book — three vowel families in one drill

hook.title: Three Bridges, Six Words
hook.content: IJs, uit, duizend, bruin, muis, boek. Ice, out, thousand, brown, mouse, book. Three vowel bridges, six everyday words, one recognition habit.

pattern.title: Read the digraph, not the English letter
pattern.content: IJ is one sound, /ɛi/. UI is one sound, /œy/. OE is one sound, /u/. The English spelling on the other side is a memory hook; the Dutch sound is the target.
pattern.trap_note: Do not pronounce ui as 'oo-ee' in two beats. It is one gliding vowel, closer to a rounded 'ow' with the tongue forward.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (IJ / UI / OE Gym):
exercises.target_answer: het ijs, uit, duizend, bruin, de muis, het boek
exercises.meaning: ice, out, thousand, brown, mouse, book
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "IJ / UI / OE Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “The ice is cold.”?
exercises.explanation: “Het ijs is koud.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “IJ / UI / OE Gym”.

cues: The pattern: Read the digraph, not the English letter
exercises.explanation: “Ik ga uit.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Read the digraph, not the English letter.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Do not pronounce ui as 'oo-ee' in two beats. It is one gliding vowel, closer to a rounded 'ow' with the tongue forward.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
options: not A thousand books are many.
exercises.explanation: “Duizend boeken zijn veel.” is word-for-word “A thousand books are many.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Read the digraph, not the English letter.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: The mouse is brown.
exercises.explanation: “De muis is bruin.” reuses only material taught in “IJ / UI / OE Gym” — Read the digraph, not the English letter.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “De muis is bruin.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Read the digraph, not the English letter.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “The book is brown.”
twist.explanation: Boek brings the oe bridge back after the ui words; the frame is unchanged.

summary.outcome: Produce six words across the ij, ui and oe families without mixing the sounds.
summary.takeaway: One gliding vowel per digraph; do not split it into two English beats.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: G, CH & Dutch Spelling.

ijs.etymology_derivation: English ice and Dutch ijs are the same word.

uit.etymology_derivation: The ui digraph answers to English ou: out, house, mouse.

duizend.etymology_derivation: English thousand and Dutch duizend are the same word.

bruin.etymology_derivation: English brown and Dutch bruin are the same word.

muis.etymology_derivation: English mouse and Dutch muis are the same word.

boek.etymology_derivation: English book and Dutch boek share the spelling bridge; Dutch oe is /u/.

vowel_ij.name: The IJ Bridge
vowel_ij.phonetic_rule: Dutch ij is /ɛi/ and often answers to English i/y: ice → ijs, wine → wijn, five → vijf.
vowel_ij.historical_linguistics: The digraph ij spells a Dutch diphthong; English orthography kept a different vowel from the same Germanic stock.
vowel_ij.philological_note: IJ is two letters but one sound. It is not English /aɪ/.
